transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been making mistakes at work that I really should not be making. I’m a camera operator and editor, and lately I’ll label camera cards wrong, miss a timecode note, or export a client cut with the wrong lower-third—even after I thought I checked it. It feels like dumb technical stuff I know better than to mess up, and it’s starting to scare me.
Have you had trouble paying attention and making careless mistakes like this since childhood?

Yeah, I think it goes back pretty far. In elementary school, teachers would move my desk around because I was always getting out of my seat, blurting out answers, or bothering other kids before I even realized I was doing it.
Do these kinds of attention mistakes also happen regularly outside of work?

It does, yeah, though work is where it’s most obvious because there are so many details to track. But the same kind of thing happens in regular life too—like I’ll think I’ve checked something and then realize I missed an obvious detail. The work mistakes are just what finally scared me, because I know how to label cards and check timecodes and lower-thirds, and I’m still messing them up.
Besides work, what’s one everyday situation where this same kind of attention slip causes a problem for you?

I guess the everyday version is the same kind of thing, just lower stakes. Like I’ll think I checked something, but I missed the obvious detail. At work it’s labeling a camera card wrong or missing a timecode note, and outside work it’s that same feeling of, “How did I not catch that?” even when I thought I was being careful.
Have these attention mistakes caused problems in your relationships?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I can imagine it’s annoying sometimes if I miss something or have to go back and fix it, but I don’t know that I’d say it’s caused a major relationship problem. At least nothing specific is coming to mind.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks once you’ve started them?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t have a clear example coming to mind where I start something and just can’t finish it. I mean, I’m sure I put things down and come back to them later sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s often enough that I’d call it a real problem.
Do you still often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still even when you need to?

Yeah, I do. Like in a client screening, when I’m supposed to just sit there and watch quietly, it can feel like this pressure building under my skin. I’m sitting still on the outside, but inside I really feel like I need to get up or move or do something with my body.
Have these attention or restlessness problems ever gotten you in trouble at school or work?

Yeah, at work it has. Not like I got formally written up, but my producers have started trusting me less on more complicated shoots. I can tell they’re more hesitant to put me on things where there are a lot of moving parts. And that’s been affecting my chance of moving up into a senior director of photography role, even though I think the actual quality of my camera work is good.
Have you had any head injury or neurological illness that seemed to affect your concentration or thinking?
Not that I know of. I haven’t had a head injury or any neurological illness that I’m aware of that changed my concentration or thinking.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about work stuff when there’s a real reason, but I wouldn’t say I spend a lot of time worrying about a bunch of different things for no clear reason.
